rows.text: Under Article 25(2) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 and Annex I, Part A, the six categories listed there always require a procedure involving a notified body (module B followed by C, module H, or module G).

value: module B followed by module C (EU type-examination plus internal production control)
rows.text: Under Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 (REG.md), Article 25(2), for machinery in categories listed in Annex I, Part A, the manufacturer may choose one of module B followed by module C, module H, or module G.

rows.value: Annex I, Part A, point 5: safety components with fully or partially self-evolving behaviour using machine learning approaches ensuring safety functions
rows.text: Under Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 (REG.md), Annex I, Part A, point 5 places a safety component with fully or partially self-evolving machine-learning behaviour ensuring safety functions in the category of Part A procedure products.

rows.value: Interlocking movable guards are required instead of fixed guards for moving transmission parts where frequent access is envisaged (Regulation, Annex III, point 1.3.8.1).
rows.text: Under Annex III, point 1.3.8.1 of the Regulation, guards for moving transmission parts must be interlocking movable guards rather than fixed guards where frequent access is envisaged. The Directive's Annex I, 1.3.8.1 says 'should' for the same case, but the Regulation's 'shall' is the binding wording relied on here.

value: risks of contact which could lead to accidents
risks of contact leading to hazardous situations
psychological stress that may be caused by the interaction with the machinery
rows.text: Annex III, point 1.3.7 of the Regulation (REG.md) addresses risks related to moving parts: contact risks that could lead to accidents, accidental blockage of moving parts, contact risks leading to hazardous situations, and psychological stress from interaction with the machinery.

rows.value: The natural or legal person who carries out the substantial modification of the machinery (not a non-professional user modifying it for its own use) is considered the manufacturer under Article 18 of the Regulation.
rows.text: Under Article 18 (Other cases in which obligations of manufacturers apply) of the Machinery Regulation (REG.md), the natural or legal person that carries out a substantial modification is treated as the manufacturer and must ensure and declare conformity on its sole responsibility.

value: the information set out in Annex III
the EU declaration of conformity set out in Annex V, Part A (or an internet address or machine-readable code where it can be accessed in the instructions for use)
rows.text: Under Regulation (EU) 2023/1230, Article 10(7) and 10(8) (REG.md), manufacturers must ensure that machinery is accompanied by the instructions for use, the information in Annex III, and the EU declaration of conformity in Annex V, Part A, or alternatively an internet address or machine-readable code giving access to that declaration in the instructions for use.

The manufacturer must keep the technical documentation and the EU declaration of conformity at the disposal of market surveillance authorities for at least 10 years after the machinery or related product has been placed on the market or put into service (REG Art. 10(3)); the older Directive 2006/42/EC, Annex II point 2, also gives at least 10 years but counts from the last date of manufacture.

Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 applies from 20 January 2027 under Article 54 (Entry into force and application), as corrected by Corrigendum point 10; some specific articles apply earlier under the same article.

Yes. Directive 2006/42/EC is repealed with effect from 20 January 2027 (Regulation Art. 51(2), as corrected by the corrigendum), so on 16 January 2027 conforming machinery can still be placed on the market.

rows.value: INAIL carries out the first periodic verification of Annex VII equipment, within sixty days from the request (DM 11 April 2011, art. 2, c. 1); the INAIL guide's 45-day figure is overridden by this law.
rows.text: Under DM 11 April 2011, art. 2, c. 1, INAIL is responsible for the first periodic verification of the Annex VII work equipment, to be carried out within sixty days from the request. The INAIL guide's 45 days from receipt of the complete request is guidance and ranks below this law.
Under D.Lgs. 81/2008, art. 71, c. 9, the employer must keep at least the results of the last three years of the checks under c. 8 and make them available to the supervisory bodies.

All MAHA MA STAR two-post lift models in the EC declaration (manual section 10) are vehicle servicing lifts under REG Annex I, Part A, point 3, so from 20 January 2027 (REG Art. 54, corrected) they need the Article 25(2) procedure with a notified body; the transitional rule in Art. 52(1) covers only products placed on the market before that date.

The documents do not mention a model RC-5 anywhere, so no conformity assessment procedure for it can be determined from them; the generic Machinery Regulation rules (Art. 25) would need the model's category in Annex I to apply.

The files do not state CS-400's category under Annex I of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230, so they cannot say whether internal production control (module A, Article 25(3)(a) or 25(4)) remains available to it after 20 January 2027, when Directive 2006/42/EC is repealed (Article 51(2), as corrected by the corrigendum).

rows.text: Annex III, section 1.1.9 ('Protection against corruption') of the Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 is the essential requirement the Directive 2006/42/EC does not contain; the Directive's Annex I, 1.2.1 covers only faults and errors in control systems.

rows.value: The ASL carries out the subsequent periodic verifications at the employer's free choice; ARPA does so where a regional law provides for it; authorised public or private bodies may also do them (D.Lgs. 81/2008, art. 71, c. 11).
rows.text: Under D.Lgs. 81/2008, art. 71, c. 11, the successive verifications of Annex VII equipment are done at the employer's free choice by the ASL, or by ARPA where a regional law so provides, or by authorised public or private subjects; DM2011, art. 2, c. 1 likewise makes the ASL the holder of the successive verifications, but the D.Lgs. prevails over the DM.
